title: Lexie
description: An AI agent that makes the contractor calls you don't want to make. Describe the problem in a chat thread and Lexie fans out real outbound calls to local vendors in parallel, quotes the same scope to each one, negotiates the appointment, and books it. Every call is recorded and transcribed, and nothing dials until you confirm.

title: Parallely
description: Parallely earned 240+ GitHub stars from the developer community. It's a CLI I built that splits one large coding task into sections and runs them concurrently, one AI coding agent per section, all in a shared git worktree. A fullscreen TUI streams every agent's live progress, output, and token usage, and finished sections auto-commit to a shared integration branch. Backend-agnostic: it drives Codex, Claude Code, or OpenCode.

title: MycelicMemory
description: I built MycelicMemory, an MCP server that gives any coding agent a robust, semantically indexed, knowledge-graph-backed memory system that is fully local and secure. Sub-100ms hybrid search, automatic capture from your coding sessions, zero cloud dependency, and it works with Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, or any MCP client. I always use it when I code.

title: Traceview
description:
A flight recorder for browser agents. Agents like Browser Use and Claude in Chrome crash on step 7 of a 12-step workflow and leave you with a stack trace that explains nothing. Traceview captures every step as the agent runs — the DOM before and after, screenshots with a compare slider, the exact prompt the model saw, and the token cost of each call — then replays it in a local-first viewer. One line of instrumentation, SQLite plus flat files under your home dir, no cloud and no phone-home.

I run Traceview on every project I build, because the audit trail it captures becomes a substrate I can reason on top of: I mine the recorded runs for patterns and turn them into self-improving suggestions, each surfaced as a human-approval ticket that, once I sign off, is handed to a sandboxed Claude Code session that implements it. The same trail drives debugging — when an error surfaces anywhere in my agentic pipelines, Traceview pins it to the exact step that failed, and I convert that into a bug-fix ticket and then into a prompt for a sandboxed Claude Code session running in an isolated git worktree that lands the fix.
